assertions.description: The Notification interface is exposed on Window.
Notification.permission returns one of the spec's NotificationPermission values: default, denied, or granted.
The Permissions API resolves a query for the notifications permission with a valid state.
requireInteraction remains a Notification instance member (the macOS change ignores it OS-side for app notifications; the IDL surface is unchanged).
The Badging API methods setAppBadge and clearAppBadge exist on navigator (their macOS contract now requires notifications permission to display).
The display-mode media feature used to detect installed-PWA context evaluates: exactly one of standalone/window-controls-overlay/minimal-ui/fullscreen/browser matches.

With chrome://flags/#enable-mac-pwas-notification-attribution enabled on macOS Chrome 130+, a notification fired from an installed PWA appears in Notification Center under the PWA's own name and icon (its App Shim), not under Google Chrome.
assertions.test: OS-level attribution cannot be observed from JavaScript: it requires macOS, Chrome 130+, an installed PWA, the enable-mac-pwas-notification-attribution flag, granted notification permission, and a human looking at Notification Center.
